It is fully inked, a clean wedge with a short tail, at the height of the page's apostrophes (compare d'en on the same line), only smaller; read as a stray apostrophe sort rather than a speck and transcribed as printed. A stray/turned comma sort is the alternative explanation; either way it is type.

uncertain.note: the word-break sign after 'iour' (iour|nee) is not a level dash like 'troi-' (blocks[0].lines[2]) but a small drop-shaped point raised to mid x-height (body-7.jpg, 2nd line end, 4x). The same raised mid-height point ends 'preu-' (blocks[6].lines[1]) and 'arri-' (blocks[6].lines[2]) and follows TEXTE; it is this page's alternative break sort. Transcribed as '-' per §1 (any line-end word-break sign), consistent with 'preu-' and 'arri-'. Reader A read this one as a point sort ('iour.').

uncertain.note: sic: 'Encor' is set as two words with a full word space; transcribed as printed. No break sign after 'neceſſai' (runs on to 're').

uncertain.note: sic, wrong sort: 'cuy' for 'ouy'. At 3x (body-7.jpg, last line) the first sort is an open c with two inward terminals, exactly like the c of 'ce' on the line, while the o of 'auoir' just before is a closed ring. Both readers agree; transcribed as printed. Line-end break sign is the raised mid-height point (see blocks[4].lines[8]).

uncertain.text: ue point {a2} toutesfois quãd le vray Martin Guerre arri-
uncertain.note: the marker is the page's second 'a' (the alphabet restarts at ANNOT. XXXIII), keyed a2 per §4. The first r of 'arri' is over-inked but is an r (compare rr of 'Guerre'). Line-end break sign is the raised mid-height point.
the print sets 'ex.' then a small gap then a level dash at the line end (the break sign for 'ex-|ceſ.'); the period before it is a separate round dot. Spaced per §1; both readers agree.
'prelato' is printed with a plain italic e, not the æ ligature; sic.

the key letter b is followed by a round point before 'Accurſe'; the point is taken as belonging to the key and not included in lines. The note is printed beside the TEXTE heading, so beside_line is null.
sic: a level mid-height dash (hyphen), not a period, follows 'quinto', with a word space before 'D.'; transcribed as printed. Both readers agree.

the note's key letter is a heavily blotted italic sort (margin-3.jpg, bottom, 4x): a blob with the outline of an italic a. Read as 'a' (keyed a2) because the body marker it answers (blocks[6].lines[2]) is a clear italic a and the alphabet restarts at ANNOT. XXXIII; a coincidence of ink rather than a different letter. The note begins in the gap between 'nee de S. Laurens.' and the ANNOT. XXXIII heading, ahead of its marker line, so beside_line is null.
the print sets 'e x' with a gap; joined per §1. A comma, not a period, follows the c.

three points. (1) sic, wrong sort: 'rutela' for 'tutela' — at 4x (margin-4.jpg, top line) the first sort is a short italic r with a shoulder and no crossbar, unlike the crossed t two sorts later. (2) With line 2 the reference reads 'de-|ſti.' ('deſti.'), apparently a contraction or error for 'de teſti.'; transcribed as printed. (3) A period is printed after the final 'de' (a baseline dot, clear at 4x); reader B omitted it.
